Animism (from Latin: anima, meaning 'breath', 'spirit', or 'life') is the worldview or perception that various types of natural phenomena ... possess distinct spiritual essences, souls, or personhood.

The accepted definition of animism was developed only in the late 19th century (1871) by Edward Tylor. ... soul, spirit, or sentience exists not only in humans but also in other animals, plants, rocks, geographic features (such as mountains and rivers) ... Examples include water spirits, vegetation deities, and tree spirits
